target_customer: Patients with chronic diseases in India who need monthly medicine refills, and the physicians and pharmacies that serve them
problem: Chronic patients in India buy recurring medicines at neighborhood pharmacies at full price and often fail to reorder on time. Digi-Prex takes prescriptions over WhatsApp and delivers monthly supplies at a discount.
business_model: Subscription pharmacy: margin on medicines bought direct from distributors, with some margin shared with physicians and pharmacies
product_category: Online subscription pharmacy for chronic care

founders.name: Samarth Sindhi
prior_employers: A U.S. healthcare firm (unnamed in TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Sept 2019) calls him a Brown University alum who worked for a U.S. healthcare firm before returning to India.

competitors.name: mChemist
competitors.what: Online pharmacy aimed at home delivery of chronic medicines
competitors.traction_then: Launched in 2015 as a self described first true online pharmacy in India

competitors.name: Pillofy
competitors.what: E-pharmacy focused on the chronic disease segment with refill reminders
competitors.traction_then: Described in a December 2015 article as India's first chronic segment e-pharmacy

technical_complexity.rationale: WhatsApp based ordering with recurring scheduling; the hard parts are operational (sourcing, delivery, regulation) not software.

defensibility.rationale: Recurring prescriptions and physician relationships create mild lock-in, but pharmacies and large e-pharmacies can offer refills.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large e-pharmacies later offered refill subscriptions per their own pages; Digi-Prex stayed active and spun out a clinic business, Good Health Clinic.

market_need_then: TechCrunch described thousands of customers in Hyderabad within seven months of starting, buying recurring medicines for chronic conditions, and a 15 percent discount claim to neighborhood pharmacies on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses digi-prex.com with a hyphen; the site also writes Digiprex.

identity.logo: Logo image of the Digiprex wordmark, style not described
identity.visual_style: Simple website built with a website builder per its footer
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain value messaging: cheaper than your neighborhood pharmacy with free home delivery

brand_strength.rationale: Hyphenated and inconsistently spelled name with a basic website; press covered the funding and WhatsApp model rather than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Digi-Prex launched in Hyderabad in early 2019, joined YC Summer 2019 and raised a 5.5M seed led by Khosla in September 2019 on the strength of thousands of WhatsApp ordered chronic medicine customers. It remains active with 32 listed staff and a clinic subsidiary, but no later parent round was found and a shutdown or exit was not reported.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch, Inc42, YourStory and KrASIA listings in search results; investor list from TechCrunch. A June 2021 YourStory headline says Digi-Prex's Good Health Clinic raised 5.2M led by Khosla Ventures; that article returned 403 so it is not recorded as a round of the parent. Aggregator revenue of 18.74M for FY2023 is unverified. YC page lists founding 2019 while a registry profile says the Telangana company was incorporated May 2018. Competitor sources are from 2015, before the batch. Only one founder is named by YC and TechCrunch.
